A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On Optimal Steering to Achieve Exact Fairness. Their main text, eight figures, equations, Appendices A–D and checklists support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original Gaussian simulations, Bias in Bios classification experiments and LLM emotion-steering results, with additional analyses in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations and LLM experiments in Sections 5–6 and the additional results in Appendices C–D.

M1.justification: The EF Affirmative and all-subgroup interventions, affine representation transformations and steering-vector mixing procedure are retained. The expanded optimization display in Section 4 presents the existing formulation; no algorithmic revision is described.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Gaussian distributions, profession prediction on Bias in Bios, and joyful generation of horror and comedy reviews. The additional Gaussian scenarios in Appendix C are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the original distributions or representations, Mean Matching, MiMiC, LEACE and original Gaussian Concept Steering where applicable. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The Gaussian thresholds, Llama model configurations, steering strength a = 0.03, sampling procedures and evaluation prompts remain unchanged. Section 7's expanded finite-sample discussion does not revise the experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Both retain the steering-strength mixing analysis in Figure 4, Gaussian case studies in Figures 5–7, and the Bios analysis relaxing the equal-group-probability assumption in Figure 8. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the same statistical reporting, including the checklist's acknowledgment of absent error bars or significance analysis. Appendix D.2's 50 resampling iterations for estimating steering-vector distributions are unchanged; the new high-probability discussion adds no empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figures 1–8 retain their numerical results and trends, including the reported Bios accuracy range of 0.77–0.79 and the joyfulness-versus-mixing curve. No result entries are added, removed or corrected in the appendices.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, results and proof arguments are unchanged. Appendix equations are reformatted, with some inverse factors rewritten as equivalent fractions. Section 4's added display restates the existing objective and constraints rather than introducing new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1 contribution list and concluding summary retain the claims about ideal distributions, parametric optimization and LLM steering. The expanded discussion does not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly emphasizes that Gaussian assumptions may poorly fit real data, interprets the KL gap as a measure of data bias, and discusses moment estimation, invertible transformations and bounded-moment alternatives. These provide additional applicability qualifications and interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix D's code hyperlink changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to the author-named GitHub repository mohitsharma29/Optimal-Steering. The documented implementation procedures, prompts and parameters are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Six references are added, including Eftekhari and Papyan, Theisen et al., and Wick et al. They contextualize Section 7's discussion of Gaussian representations, extensions beyond parametric assumptions and fairness under data bias. Existing cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands the exposition in Sections 4 and 7 and updates the acknowledgments with additional funding information. The remaining narrative and the main-text and appendix organization are largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a main-text optimization display, splits and realigns long equations in Appendices A–B, and relocates Figure 2 from page 7 to page 8. The eight figures retain their graphical content; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Section 7 provides clearer qualifications about Gaussian applicability and more concrete discussion of extensions, while reformatted appendix equations improve readability. These modest gains are tempered by transcription defects in the new Section 4 display, including a missing addition sign and untilded constraint parameters. The underlying proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
